OMIM:612164.summary_plain: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 4 is linked to changes in STXBP1. Research papers show these changes usually make the protein work less. Some records also show related patient studies and a few look-alike conditions, but those look-alikes are only hints, not proof of the same cause.

steps.text: Research papers show STXBP1 can cause this condition. The record links STXBP1 to Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 4.

Several papers say STXBP1 changes may make the protein work less. One report says heterozygous loss-of-function mutations were involved. Another says de novo heterozygous changes led to haploinsufficiency, which means too little working protein.
Records also show STXBP1-related studies are underway. These include a trial-readiness study, a natural history study, and a registry study for this condition.
A few other conditions look similar in symptoms. These similarities are only suggestions, not proof of a shared cause.

uncertainties: The look-alike conditions are hypothesis-only, so they do not prove shared biology.
The study records mention STXBP1 in titles or keywords, but the notes say you should confirm exact scope.
We do not have details here about which specific STXBP1 changes were found in each person.
We do not have treatment results from the listed studies.
